summary: Molnupiravir (LAGEVRIO) is an orally administered prodrug of the ribonucleoside analogue NHC (beta-D-N4-hydroxycytidine) with antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2. It is used for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults at high risk of progression to severe disease, started as soon as possible after diagnosis and within 5 days of symptom onset. It works by viral lethal mutagenesis (error catastrophe): NHC is incorporated by the viral RNA polymerase, producing an accumulation of errors in the viral genome that inhibits replication. It is given as 800 mg every 12 hours for 5 days. Key warnings include embryo-fetal toxicity (it is not recommended in pregnancy), potential effects on bone and cartilage growth (not authorized in patients under 18 years), and contraceptive advice for both sexes. In the United States it has been made available under FDA Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) rather than full approval.
indications: Treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults with a positive SARS-CoV-2 test who are at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19, including hospitalization or death, and for whom alternative authorized COVID-19 treatment options are not accessible or clinically appropriate
Should be initiated as soon as possible after a diagnosis of COVID-19 and within 5 days of symptom onset

Swallow capsules whole; do not open, crush or break

moa: Molnupiravir is a prodrug metabolized to the cytidine nucleoside analogue NHC, which distributes into cells and is phosphorylated to the active ribonucleoside triphosphate NHC-TP. NHC-TP is incorporated (as NHC-monophosphate) into SARS-CoV-2 RNA by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (nsp12), causing an accumulation of errors in the viral genome that inhibits replication - a mechanism known as viral error catastrophe or lethal mutagenesis.

absolute: No contraindications identified based on the limited available data under the EUA
relative: Patients under 18 years of age (potential effect on bone/cartilage growth)

preg: Based on findings from animal reproduction studies, molnupiravir may cause fetal harm and is not recommended for use during pregnancy. There are no human data to evaluate the risk of birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal/fetal outcomes. If considered for a pregnant individual, the prescriber must discuss known and potential benefits and risks. Females of reproductive potential should use a reliable method of contraception during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose. A pregnancy surveillance program exists for exposures during pregnancy.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with molnupiravir and for 4 days after the final dose, because there are no data on its presence in human milk, effects on the breastfed infant, or effects on milk production.
renal: No dosage adjustment is recommended in patients with renal impairment, including those on hemodialysis.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is recommended in patients with hepatic impairment.

major: No major drug interactions identified based on the limited available data under the EUA
moderate: No clinical drug-drug interaction studies have been conducted; clinically meaningful interactions are not expected based on metabolism (NHC is not a CYP substrate and the drug is not a significant CYP inhibitor/inducer)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with alcohol has been identified.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference described.

rare: Rash, urticaria and other allergic reactions reported post-authorization

monitoring: Clinical course and resolution of COVID-19 symptoms
Reproductive counseling and contraception adherence in patients of reproductive potential
Emergence of unexpected adverse events (limited clinical data)
counsel: Take all four capsules every 12 hours for the full 5 days, even if you feel better
Start the medicine within 5 days of your first COVID-19 symptoms
This medicine is not recommended during pregnancy; women who could become pregnant should use birth control during and for 4 days after treatment
Men with female partners of childbearing potential should use a reliable contraceptive method during and for at least 3 months after the last dose
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose; continue isolation as advised
pk: Antiviral activity over the 5-day treatment course; NHC is the primary circulating analyte
NHC plasma Tmax approximately 1.5 hours after oral dosing
NHC apparent terminal half-life approximately 3.3 hours
Twice-daily dosing for 5 days maintains antiviral exposure
Store capsules at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions 15-30 C permitted
pearls: In the United States molnupiravir is provided under FDA Emergency Use Authorization (EUA), not full approval - it has not received standard FDA marketing approval
Must be started within 5 days of symptom onset to be effective; reserved for high-risk patients when preferred agents are unsuitable
Not authorized in patients under 18 years because of potential effects on bone and cartilage growth
Not recommended in pregnancy; advise contraception for both sexes during and after treatment
Has a low drug-interaction burden compared with ritonavir-boosted antivirals, which can be clinically useful in polypharmacy
missed: If a dose is missed within 10 hours of when it is usually taken, take it as soon as possible and resume the normal schedule. If it has been more than 10 hours, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not double the dose.
overdose: There is no human experience of overdose. Treatment should consist of general supportive measures, including monitoring of the patient's clinical status. Hemodialysis is not expected to effectively remove NHC.
